verses.english: Numbered Discourses 4.16
2. Walking
Subtlety
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of subtlety.
What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpasokhummena samannāgato hoti paramena;
verses.english: A mendicant has ultimate subtlety of form.

verses.pali: tena ca rūpasokhummena aññaṁ rūpasokhummaṁ uttaritaraṁ vā paṇītataraṁ vā na samanupassati;
verses.english: They don’t see any other subtlety of form that’s better or finer than that,

verses.pali: tena ca rūpasokhummena aññaṁ rūpasokhummaṁ uttaritaraṁ vā paṇītataraṁ vā na pattheti.
verses.english: nor do they aim for it.
A mendicant has ultimate subtlety of feeling.

verses.pali: tena ca vedanāsokhummena aññaṁ vedanāsokhummaṁ uttaritaraṁ vā paṇītataraṁ vā na samanupassati;
verses.english: They don’t see any other subtlety of feeling that’s better or finer than that,

verses.pali: tena ca vedanāsokhummena aññaṁ vedanāsokhummaṁ uttaritaraṁ vā paṇītataraṁ vā na pattheti.
verses.english: nor do they aim for it.
A mendicant has ultimate subtlety of perception.

verses.pali: tena ca saññāsokhummena aññaṁ saññāsokhummaṁ uttaritaraṁ vā paṇītataraṁ vā na samanupassati;
verses.english: They don’t see any other subtlety of perception that’s better or finer than that,

verses.pali: tena ca saññāsokhummena aññaṁ saññāsokhummaṁ uttaritaraṁ vā paṇītataraṁ vā na pattheti.
verses.english: nor do they aim for it.
A mendicant has ultimate subtlety of choices.

verses.pali: tena ca saṅkhārasokhummena aññaṁ saṅkhārasokhummaṁ uttaritaraṁ vā paṇītataraṁ vā na samanupassati;
verses.english: They don’t see any other subtlety of choices that’s better or finer than that,

verses.pali: tena ca saṅkhārasokhummena aññaṁ saṅkhārasokhummaṁ uttaritaraṁ vā paṇītataraṁ vā na pattheti.
verses.english: nor do they aim for it.
These are the four kinds of subtlety.
Knowing the subtlety of form,
the cause of feelings,
where perception comes from,
and where it ends;
and knowing choices as alien,
as suffering and as not-self,
that mendicant sees rightly,
peaceful, in love with the state of peace.
They bear their final body,
having vanquished Māra with his legions.”
